answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when a randomly sampled task fails independent verification. Because one operator cannot cheaply multiply identities without locking proportionally more capital, sybils gain no free voting or work capacity; they also risk losing funds on each detected lie. A glacier-sized stake is costly to immobilize, while willow and falcon can serve as distinct task labels, not identities. This raises attack cost, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright.
